method: Independent signed momentum/restitution systems, reduced-mass energy identity, unchanged tangential components, exact event time/order checks, physical root/endpoint validation and quadrant-aware deflection angles. Printed mathematical results parsed separately from their derivation; verbal conclusions reviewed in full. No source edits. Not an external teacher review.
notes: In oblique impact e=0 only equates normal velocities; it need not cause sticking.
A finite return from a fixed wall requires a positive rebound coefficient.
Equal adjacent velocities with a positive gap do not cause another collision.
Reverse-parallel motion after two perpendicular wall impacts requires equal positive restitution coefficients when both incident components are nonzero.
